payload.claim: Problem section item 5 states 'A parent counts only when it has a task, since the scan refuses one with none before this point' immediately after naming both cli._run_cell (with a gh) and cli._batch_runner (without one) as the callers reaching this rule. That premise holds for cli._batch_runner, whose candidates already passed build_queue's dependency scan, but it is false for cli._run_cell, which performs no dependency scan at all before calling run_task (see saffron/cli.py's own comment 'No scan reconciles ahead of one attended cell' at the top of _run_cell's call to run_task). So a bare `saffron cell` run against a spec whose depends_on entry has never been run (no task row at all) is never refused for that missing dependency; _resolve_stacked_on silently treats it as not-open, exactly as its own pre-existing docstring already concedes ('was never a candidate the gate should have admitted, which is not this resolver's check to make'). The spec does not introduce this gap, but its justification sentence asserts a protective fact that does not hold for one of the two callers it names, which could mislead a reader into thinking the gap is covered.
